meta.title: There's an 'Island' at Coordinate Zero, Zero -- And It's Not Real
meta._convention: One scene-spec JSON per script, saved alongside it as <script-name>.scenes.json. Each beat's `duration` is intentionally omitted -- build_video.js fills it in at render time from the ACTUAL measured length of that beat's generated narration WAV.
meta._note: Null Island is pure ocean at [0,0] with no land and no country polygon at all -- highlight stays [] every beat, per README's 'scenes that aren't a country' pattern. The most literal case in the lineup: nothing here but water, a marker, and (in reality) a buoy.

beats.voText: Mapping software sometimes shows an island exactly at zero degrees latitude, zero degrees longitude, sitting in open ocean. It's not real.
It's nicknamed Null Island, what happens when broken location data defaults to that coordinate origin point and gets plotted like a real place.
beats.onScreenText: Broken data. Plotted as a place.

beats.voText: It sits in the Gulf of Guinea, off West Africa, the nearest real coastline is still hundreds of miles away in every direction.
beats.onScreenText: Hundreds of miles from any coast.

beats.voText: The only thing actually there is a real scientific buoy, quietly collecting ocean and weather data for researchers.
So many broken records point here that mapmakers gave it its own joke flag, some databases have even listed it with a population.
beats.onScreenText: Its own flag. A fake population.

beats.voText: No land, no people, just a coordinate, a buoy, and a running joke among mapmakers everywhere. Follow for more places on Earth that shouldn't exist, but do.
